dedupe_keys.name: grip4 global roads inventory project dataset vector roads and road density rasters

description: The Global Roads Inventory Project (GRIP) dataset is a consistent global roads dataset built for global environmental and biodiversity models such as GLOBIO. GRIP4 harmonises many public road sources, including OpenStreetMap, to the UNSDI-Transportation data model and classifies roads into five types, from highways to local roads. It was produced for the GLOBIO model and described by Meijer and co-authors in Environmental Research Letters (2018), which also gives future road infrastructure projections under the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways and country tables in its supplement. Coverage is global, in seven regions. The data are free under a CC0 licence and available to download from the GLOBIO website or Zenodo as a global file geodatabase and regional geodatabases and shapefiles, plus global road density rasters at 5 arcminutes (about 8 km) for all roads and each road type as ASCII grids. Caveats: the source dates and completeness vary by country, it is not suitable for navigation, and it holds no traffic or condition attributes. It supports global and regional hazard exposure screening of road networks, accessibility and planning scenarios for future roads. It complements the gROADS global roads dataset and is related to the Congo Basin forest roads map.
